display: Third-generation laksa hawker in Singapore. The stall's recipe dates from 1962, and I grind the rempah by hand every Monday.

signals.text: Tourists keep asking to take some of my paste home. It has happened three times in one month, and I have never packaged it.
I would like to know whether I am allowed to sell paste in jars, and how to do it properly, but I don't know where to start.
My hawker-centre lease ends in 2027 and none of my kids want the stall. I'm looking for a way to hand it on that doesn't end the stall.
A food blogger's write-up doubled my Saturday customers and the cockles ran out by 1pm. I want to handle busy days without changing what we sell.
I grind paste by hand for two hours every Monday at 5am and it takes a toll on my hands. I'd like to make that work lighter without using a blender.
Prawn prices keep rising and I won't raise the bowl price, because my regulars are mostly retired. I'm looking for ways to absorb the cost.
My son asked me why I do this, and I didn't know what to say. I want to find a way to explain the stall to a child who doesn't care for it.
Other hawkers my age, like my neighbour Uncle Tan, have no successor either. I'd like to talk to people who have worked through this.
My hands ache in the evenings and I worry about arthritis. I'm putting off getting it checked.
I feel guilty that the stall may end with me, and I think about it most Mondays.
My 81-year-old father is recovering from knee surgery. I'm balancing visits to him with the stall and the family.
I have only 30 minutes between lunch and dinner for any visitor, video or conversation.

offers.text: A laksa stall with a 1962 recipe: coconut-based gravy, hand-ground rempah, cockles and prawns.
Three generations of knowledge about running a neighbourhood hawker stall in Singapore, including the daily routine and the regulars.
Hands-on technique with a stone mortar, big pots and charcoal-fired stock. I can show visitors how the rempah is ground and why a blender makes it bitter.
Relationships with wet-market suppliers for galangal, lemongrass and dried shrimp. I know what to look for in each.
Twenty years of regular customers and a growing flow of tourists. I can tell you what people actually ask for and notice about the stall.
A short window between lunch and dinner for a visit, tasting or filming, if the format is small and quiet.
Experience of the hawker-centre tenancy and lease-renewal process with NEA, and of how it works when children don't take over.
A story worth telling: a stall running since 1962 and a founder's recipe that is still made by hand every Monday.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a tourist who ate at your stall. Could I buy a small jar of your laksa paste to take home?
catchers.can: He can say honestly that he has never packaged it. If a proper route exists, he may be open to a small, carefully made jar.
catchers.confirm: Do you want a small amount of paste for personal use, as opposed to a mass-market product carrying his name?

catchers.hypo: I help small food businesses in Singapore get paste or sauce packaged and compliant, in small batches. Would you want to talk?
catchers.can: He can share what he makes weekly and what he will and won't compromise on (hand-ground, no blender). He can discuss whether a small-batch jar is possible.
catchers.confirm: Can your process work with a hand-ground paste, with no blender step and no change to the recipe?

catchers.hypo: I'm a young cook who loves traditional hawker food and wants to learn a stall from the ground up. Is there any chance of an apprenticeship?
catchers.can: He can consider teaching a serious apprentice the stall's routine. He cannot promise a succession, and the recipe's exact proportions stay private.
catchers.confirm: Are you prepared to work long hours at a stall, starting early, for an extended period?

catchers.hypo: I'm writing about hawker succession in Singapore, where the children don't want to take over. Would you talk to me?
catchers.can: He can describe the situation from experience: the 2027 lease, how the tenancy works, and what he has and hasn't found. He can also introduce a fellow hawker in the same position, Uncle Tan.
catchers.confirm: Is your piece about the hawker's real situation, rather than a nostalgic piece that skips the hard parts?

catchers.hypo: My father is also an elderly hawker with no successor and he's struggling with it. Do you know anyone who understands?
catchers.can: He can listen and talk plainly, and through Uncle Tan (same age, same situation) he can bring two older hawkers together.
catchers.confirm: Is the person looking for peer company from someone in the same position, rather than a business solution?

catchers.hypo: I'm a physiotherapist who works with older patients' recovery after knee surgery, and I'd like to share advice on staying consistent with exercises.
catchers.can: Through his 81-year-old father, who is recovering from knee surgery and complaining about his physio, he can pass on a good approach if it suits the father.
catchers.confirm: Is your advice aimed at an elderly patient recovering at home from knee surgery?

catchers.hypo: I'm a school administrator or teacher who runs a programme where children visit local workplaces, and I'd like a hawker to speak to the class.
catchers.can: Through his wife Mei Ling, who works as a school administrator, he may be able to arrange or point to someone with a school connection. He can also speak briefly himself, keeping it short.
catchers.confirm: Is this a short, low-pressure visit that fits around stall hours?

catchers.hypo: I'm a food blogger or video maker. May I film you grinding the paste on a Monday morning?
catchers.can: He can host a short, quiet shoot between lunch and dinner. A Monday 5am grinding session is possible if the crew is small and doesn't push him to talk much.
catchers.confirm: Can you work around his schedule and keep the shoot short, with no scripted talking?

catchers.hypo: I'm an arthritis or hand-health specialist. Do you have hands that ache from repetitive manual work?
catchers.can: He can take a practical conversation about hand strain from grinding and stirring. He would likely welcome advice that keeps the manual method.
catchers.confirm: Is your advice compatible with continuing to grind by hand, and not a recommendation to automate?

forbids.text: I will not use a blender for the rempah.
I will not raise the bowl price above its current level.
I cannot close the stall for more than one day a week.
I will not franchise the stall or put its name on cheap products.
I will not share the exact paste proportions.
I will not talk about finances.
I do not want to be pushed into long on-camera talking. I only have 30 minutes between lunch and dinner.
I won't put up signs or promotions to chase the crowd. We sell what we sell.

projects.name: Small-batch jar of the paste
projects.text: Explore whether a small, carefully made jar of hand-ground paste could be sold to tourists and regulars without compromising the recipe or the name.

projects.name: Stall succession
projects.text: Find a way for the stall to continue past the 2027 lease end. This could mean a trained successor who takes over the tenancy or another arrangement that keeps the stall's food.

policy.t1: When there is a real sign of collaboration, I will share that the lease ends in 2027 with no successor, how much paste I make weekly, my Monday routine and my supplier relationships.
policy.t2: Once I am fairly sure and know who I'm talking to, I will talk about my family's doubts, my worries about my hands, and my fears about the stall ending with me.
policy.never: The exact recipe proportions and my finances.
